Event 9 at 48.768 km non-reflective loss 0.13 - SC-11 at 47.622 (diff 1.146). Event 10 at 52.679 km reflective loss 0.23 - B-ODF at 51.46 plus ~1.2 km cords? Actually launch/receive cords 1 km each? Note says launch and receive cords of 1.000 km were used; receive cord ends in open connector. Distance measurement from ODF at shooting site. Hard to parse exactly but seems consistent.

No anomalous loss. Loss per km 0.235 dB/km. Total fibre length approx 51.46 km => attenuation ~12.09 dB. Commissioning loss at 1550 12.12 dB. So link loss normal.

Rx power -21.2 dBm. Tx power ~1.16 dBm average. So loss = Tx - Rx = 1.16 - (-21.2) = 22.36 dB. That's about 10 dB higher than commissioning 12.12 dB.

Since Tx normal, link loss normal per OTDR, so extra loss must be at site B, possibly attenuator.

Site notes: receiver module replaced 2026-10-19 12:22 UTC. Attenuator refitted from spares box. Alarm raised 13:00 same day. Design attenuator 0 dB. Available values 0,3,5,7,10,15. So likely wrong attenuator installed, e.g., 10 dB or 15 dB.

Calculate expected Rx power: Tx ~1.2 dBm, link loss ~12.1 dB, attenuator 0 dB => Rx ~ -10.9 dBm. Actual -21.2 dBm => extra ~10.3 dB loss. Could be 10 dB attenuator.

Let's check if any other explanation: connector dirty? Could cause a few dB. But 10 dB is too high for dirty connector. Maybe wrong attenuator.

Also OTDR from B event 1 at -0.003 km reflective loss 0.23 - likely B-ODF connector. Event 5 at 16.8 km reflective loss 0.19 - that's MID-PP from B: distance from B to MID-PP = 51.46 - 35.08 = 16.38 km. OTDR shows 16.8 km, close. No extra loss.

So root cause likely wrong attenuator installed at site B after receiver replacement.
